PROPOSAL A23: In the existing W5(c,e,f) server rehearsal, bind each game ID's independently reserved opening to the position command actually sent on that worker's engine stream before accepting its rows, including retries and a locally drawn fallback.
KIND: measurement
EVIDENCE: W5 already covers reservation replay, opening logs, packed row/content parity and receiver dedup. None of those listed plants exchanges two *different, valid* dispatched openings while leaving the reservations and receipts under their original IDs. Source/src/uci.cpp:54–82 silently returns on an unknown root and scans for the exact 'moves' token. The measured two-history case runs two actual unmodified r67 processes concurrently. With A and B exchanged both jobs end normally, still give distinct, checksummable full records and the correct expected root sgstate and first row. Under reserved A, all 67 row boards and the final board from B reconstruct from the expected root. Under correct A there are 81 rows; second row in the two games has the same move and FEN but −15 vs −30 cp. Swapping both can preserve total corpus composition if both complete. Losing just B's assigned worker after A was wrongly credited leaves B's output billed to A and A's intended result missing. These are deliberate faults in the test, with no claim of an observed failure in the PC or server launcher.
COST: Two live engine streams, two clean starts and four paired calls in the existing W5 rehearsal, no GPU or paid server. Per-game equality can be checked on the final serialized line against the immutable manifest+ID record (or equivalent binding), with no second engine search and no new engine command. Optional sgstate measured separately on 128 starts × two repeats × two arms, 512 games; rows per CPU-second +0.27% [−0.92,+1.51], wall +0.24% [−0.95,+1.48]. This observation alone misses the swapped pair. W5(g)'s existing real throughput bar still applies.
HOW IT IS JUDGED: Before the paid day, two independently reserved IDs run concurrently. Exchange their legal wire payloads, also after a worker restart. Both wrong assignments must fail before credit; a legitimate restart/retry must bind to the same reservation and earn exactly one credit. Also switch only the receipt association after two correct sends: neither result may pass under the other ID. A worker that legitimately draws locally must bind to that logged fallback under its own ID. The independent expected record, the final write to the intended process, and the corresponding result/receipt must be tied together; two hashes copied from the same mislabelled object cannot serve as a control. Existing equivalent coverage can satisfy the test. No separate production sgstate round trip required.
WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: A current W5 end-to-end fixture that already exposes both the input and receipt swaps, including retry, satisfies A23 as written. I would also withdraw a new requirement if the day does not use per-game assignment/receipt identity for recovery or deficit accounting. No claim of an Elo improvement.
 
Neon: can you independently reproduce the history swap or the distinct, valid receipts under exchanged IDs, and check whether W5 already plants both faults? Fable can wait for both votes. The receipt-only swap above is a declared gate for the actual future server implementation, not a claim that I tested its receiver.

Exact UCI protocol for the deliberate plants: on each process use the pinned r67 net, all 24 LOOP_OPTIONS, isready, ucinewgame, isready. Send 'position startpos moves '+the history, then 'sgstate', then 'selfgame softnodes 2000 evallimit 2000 maxply 300 writeminply 8 drawply 80 drawscore 5 drawcount 8'. A = b1c3 g8f6 c3d5 b8a6 g1h3 a6b8 h3g1 f6e4. B = b1c3 g8f6 c3e4 f6g8 e4c3 g8f6 c3d5 f6e4. The other plants change moves→mvoes; remove the last two A plies; and use 'startposs' after 'position startpos moves e2e4 e7e5'. Row/end digest uses LF-terminated sg and sgend lines. Timing starts are the first 128 frozen 081814Z openings; rotate the two conditions by (game+repeat) parity and resample 128 game IDs 10,000 times PCG64 seed 202611230918. Each game's four normalized transcripts agreed exactly.
